messages.subject: building cran package "lme4" for renjin.
messages.body_plain:
I need to use the R package "lme4" for mixed models but as it appears that the package is not yet built for renjin. Can someone guide me how to build CRAN packages for renjin?
Help is much appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: building cran package "lme4" for renjin.
messages.body_plain:
Hi, the latest version of lme4, is not yet built, but you can see the results of an earlier version here:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/lme4/1.1-8

Unfortunately, it looks like this package requires the Matrix package, which currently does not build under Renjin because of some problems with Renjin's implementation of S4.

S4 support in Renjin is something we will be working alot on in the coming months so stay tuned for now!

Alex

messages.subject: Renjin user survey - please help!!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
With the kick-off a 3-year EU-sponsored research project in which Renjin will play a prominent role, we're excited to be able to support Renjin development on a full-time basis. In addition to the research projects with CWI and Horizon 2020, we're exploring providing more commercial services around Renjin as we see it being used more and more in 'production.'

To this end, we'd really appreciate if you could take a moment to complete a short survey on how use (or don't use!) Renjin:

http://bit.ly/1VWXPcE

Whether you've only played with Renjin, or you're submitting pull requests regularly (thanks!) it would be great to understand your use case.

Many thanks,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible use Renjin to do Fisher Test
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible use Renjin to do Fisher Test
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wang,
Yes indeed this should work - I tested it out and it looks like one of the optimizations we've added recently is choking: there is an expression
sum(d[d <= d[x - lo + 1] * relErr])
in fisher.test() where d is a deferred execution graph and gets re-evaluated over and over again instead of getting shipped off to the parallel executor. I'll try to have a fix for this today or tomorrow.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: is 'stringr' really supported ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

stringr indeed depends on stringi and also on magrittr. All three packages currently build for Renjin (stringi didn't at the time you tried), which means that their namespaces can be loaded in Renjin. However, if you look at these packages then you will see that most tests (i.e. examples) fail therefore they cannot be actually used at this moment. We are looking into improving the wording on http://packages.renjin.org to better reflect the state of packages in Renjin and we'll include your experience in designing a better user experience.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan
